hook.line: Tomás freezes whenever he has to speak Spanish to someone who matters. A friend who just says "you can do it" doesn't help much. Naming the fear is kinder, and Vale knows exactly how to do it.
hook.en: Don't be afraid of making mistakes.

Dare to give it a try! (to a friend)

rule:
Three ways to cheer someone on:

*No tengas miedo de* + infinitive: "don't be afraid of". English says "be", Spanish says *tener* (have) fear, and the ending is *-as*, not *-es*: *tengas*.
*¡Atrévete a…!* plus an infinitive: "dare to", take the risk.
*No te rindas.* "Don't give up": keep going.

To a group, *No tengan miedo de…*. To someone you call *usted*, *No tenga miedo de…* and *No se rinda*.

Saying what the fear is (*de equivocarte*) feels warmer than a bare "you can do it".
smallPrint: Teachers call these negative commands. *Atrévete* is a *tú* command with *te* stuck to the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tengas* or *tienes*. Cheering on a friend: No ___ miedo de equivocarte. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: To tell someone "don't", the verb takes *-as*: *tengas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tengan* or *tengas*. Cheering on two friends: No ___ miedo de pedir ayuda. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: No tengan miedo de pedir ayuda.
yourTurn.why: Two people, so the group ending *-an*: *tengan*.
*No te rindas*: the little *te* stays in front after *no*.

yourTurn.prompt: Dare to give it a try! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Atrévete a* plus the infinitive, with *lo* glued onto the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Don't be afraid to tell her the truth. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No tengas miedo de decirle la verdad.
yourTurn.why: *No tengas miedo de* plus the infinitive, and *le* glued on.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: No tengas miedo de preguntar. Say it to someone you call *usted*.
Make it formal: No te rindas. Say it to someone you call *usted*.
yourTurn.why: *Te* becomes *se* and the verb ends in *-a*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tienes* only states a fact; to encourage someone, use *tengas*.
Making a mistake is *equivocarse*, so it keeps its little word: *equivocarte*.
*Atreverse* always needs *a* before the next verb.

personal: Think of someone who is nervous about something, and encourage them: *No tengas miedo de…* or *Atrévete a…*
